summary: The Beis HaMikdash had measuring cups for dry flour: an issaron and a half issaron (Rabbi Meir says two issaron cups). Flour was always measured one issaron at a time, and the half issaron was for the Kohen Gadol's daily mincha.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי מִדּוֹת שֶׁל יָבֵשׁ הָיוּ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
chunks.en: There were two measures for dry things in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: Two sizes of measuring vessels for dry substances were used in the Temple for measuring flour for the meal offerings.

chunks.en: an issaron and a half issaron.
chunks.st: One held a tenth of an ephah and the other held one-half of a tenth of an ephah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: An issaron, an issaron,
chunks.st: There were three measuring vessels; one that held a tenth of an ephah, another one that also held a tenth of an ephah,

chunks.en: and a half issaron.
chunks.st: and a third one that held one-half of a tenth of an ephah.

chunks.en: What was the issaron used for?
chunks.st: What purpose did the tenth of an ephah measuring vessel serve?

chunks.en: With it he measured for all the menachos.
chunks.st: It was the vessel with which one would measure flour for all the meal offerings.

chunks.en: He did not measure
chunks.st: One would not measure
chunks.stMore: the flour by using a measuring vessel of a size that held the entire volume of flour required at once, i.e.,

chunks.en: with a cup of three for a bull,
chunks.st: neither with a vessel of three-tenths of an ephah for the meal offering accompanying the sacrifice of a bull,

chunks.en: nor with a cup of two for a ram,
chunks.st: nor with a vessel of two-tenths of an ephah for the meal offering accompanying the sacrifice of a ram.

chunks.en: but he measured them one issaron at a time.
chunks.st: Rather, one measures the flour for them by repeatedly using the tenth of an ephah measuring vessel to measure the required number of tenths.

chunks.en: What was the half issaron used for?
chunks.st: What purpose did the one-half of a tenth of an ephah measuring vessel serve?

chunks.he: שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה מוֹדֵד חֲבִתֵּי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: With it he measured the griddle-cakes of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: It was the vessel with which one would measure the flour for the High Priest’s griddle-cake offering.

chunks.en: half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
chunks.st: A tenth of an ephah was required each day; he sacrificed half of it in the morning and the other half of it in the afternoon.

summary: There were seven measuring cups for liquids, from a hin down to a quarter log. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says one hin cup had lines marking the amounts. Rabbi Shimon says there was no hin cup, but a cup of a log and a half for the Kohen Gadol's mincha.

chunks.he: שֶׁבַע מִדּוֹת שֶׁל לַח הָיוּ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: There were seven measures for liquids in the Beis HaMikdash:
chunks.st: There were seven measuring vessels for liquids in the Temple.

chunks.en: a hin, and half a hin,
chunks.st: There was a vessel of one hin, i.e., twelve log. Three vessels were used to measure the oil and wine for the meal offerings and libations that accompanied the sacrifice of an animal. For a bull there was a vessel of one-half of a hin, i.e., six log;

chunks.en: and a third of a hin,
chunks.st: and for a ram there was one of one-third of a hin, i.e., four log;

chunks.en: and a quarter of a hin,
chunks.st: and for a lamb there was one of one-quarter of a hin, i.e., three log.

chunks.en: a log, and half a log,
chunks.st: In addition, there was a vessel that held one log to measure the oil for all standard meal offerings; and another one that held one-half of a log
chunks.stMore: for measuring the water used in the rite of a woman suspected by her husband of having been unfaithful [sota] and also for the oil used in the loaves accompanying the thanks offering (see 88a);

chunks.en: and a quarter log.
chunks.st: and another one that held one-quarter of a log
chunks.stMore: for measuring the water used in the purification of a leper and also for the oil used in the wafers and loaves that the nazirite brings on the day that his term of naziriteship ends.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer bar Tzadok says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:

chunks.en: There were lines marked on the hin cup:
chunks.st: It was not necessary to have several vessels of different sizes; rather, there were graduations [shenatot] on the vessel that held one hin indicating that

chunks.en: "Up to here is for a bull,"
chunks.st: until here is the quantity needed for the bull,

chunks.en: "up to here is for a ram,"
chunks.st: and until here is the quantity needed for the ram,

chunks.en: "up to here is for a lamb."
chunks.st: and until here is the quantity needed for the lamb.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: There was no hin cup there,
chunks.st: There was no vessel there in the Temple that held one hin,

chunks.en: for what would a hin be used for?
chunks.st: as what purpose could a one-hin vessel serve? That volume of liquid was never used in an offering.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מִדָּה יְתֵרָה שֶׁל לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה הָיְתָה,
chunks.en: Rather, there was one more cup of a log and a half,
chunks.st: Rather, there was an additional measuring vessel of one and a half log there, in the Temple, which completed the tally of seven vessels,

chunks.he: שֶׁבָּהּ הָיָה מוֹדֵד לְמִנְחַת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: with which he measured for the mincha of the Kohen Gadol:
chunks.st: with which one would measure the oil used for the griddle-cake meal offering of the High Priest;

chunks.he: לֹג וּמֶחֱצָה בַּבֹּקֶר וְלֹג וּמֶחֱצָה בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם:
chunks.en: a log and a half in the morning, and a log and a half in the afternoon.
chunks.st: one and a half log were used in the morning and one and a half log in the afternoon.

summary: The mishnah explains what the smaller cups were used for. The Sages say a mincha gets one log of oil for each issaron, but Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says every mincha gets just one log. It also lists the oil for the nesachim of a bull, ram and lamb, and for the Menorah.

chunks.en: What was the quarter log used for?
chunks.st: What purpose did the quarter-log measuring vessel serve?

chunks.en: A quarter log of water for a metzora,
chunks.st: It was used to measure a quarter-log of water for the purification of the leper,

chunks.en: and a quarter log of oil for a nazir.
chunks.st: and a quarter-log of oil for the wafers and loaves that the nazirite brings on the day that his term of naziriteship ends.

chunks.en: What was the half log used for?
chunks.st: What purpose did the half-log measuring vessel serve?

chunks.en: Half a log of water for a sotah,
chunks.st: It was used to measure a half-log of water for the rite of the sota

words.note: A woman whose husband suspected her; she drank special water.

chunks.en: and half a log of oil for the todah.
chunks.st: and a half-log of oil for the three types of loaves of matza accompanying the thanks offering.

chunks.en: And with the log cup he measured for all the menachos.
chunks.st: And with the vessel of one log, one would measure the oil for all the standard meal offerings.

chunks.en: Even a mincha of sixty issaron,
chunks.st: Each tenth of an ephah of flour requires one log of oil. Accordingly, even if one brings a meal offering of sixty tenths of an ephah of flour,

chunks.en: he puts in sixty log of oil.
chunks.st: one adds to it sixty log of oil.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: Even a mincha of sixty issaron
chunks.st: Each meal offering, irrespective of its volume, even a meal offering of sixty tenths of an ephah of flour,

chunks.en: gets only its one log,
chunks.st: requires only its single log of oil,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 14):
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to the offering brought by a poor leper on the day of his purification:

chunks.en: "for a mincha, and a log of oil."
chunks.st: “And a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil” (Leviticus 14:21).
chunks.stMore: The juxtaposition of “a meal offering” with “a log of oil” teaches a principle for all meal offerings: Each offering requires only one log of oil. The mishna lists the quantities of oil and wine that were required for the meal offerings and libations that accompanied the sacrifice of an animal.

chunks.en: Six log for a bull,
chunks.st: Six log, i.e., one-half of a hin, for those of a bull;

chunks.en: four for a ram,
chunks.st: and four log, i.e., one-third of a hin, for those of a ram;

chunks.en: three for a lamb,
chunks.st: and three log, i.e., one-quarter of a hin, for those of a lamb.

chunks.en: three and a half for the Menorah,
chunks.st: In addition, three and a half log of oil were required for the Candelabrum,

chunks.en: half a log for each lamp.
chunks.st: as there were seven lamps and a half-log was required for each lamp.

summary: Nesachim with the same amount of oil for the flour may be mixed together, but those of lambs may not be mixed with those of bulls and rams. If each was mixed with its own oil first, they are kosher. The lamb of the omer has a double mincha but regular nesachim.
stIntro: Many animal offerings are brought together with a meal offering and a wine libation. These additions are collectively referred to as libations.

chunks.en: We may mix the nesachim of rams with the nesachim of bulls,
chunks.st: One may mix together the libations of bulls with the libations of rams;
chunks.stMore: the meal offerings may be mixed as they both share the same ratio of flour to oil, i.e., two log of oil for each tenth of an ephah of flour.

chunks.en: the nesachim of lambs with the nesachim of lambs,
chunks.st: Likewise, one may mix together the libations of lambs with the libations of other lambs,
chunks.stMore: as the meal offerings both share the same ratio of three log of oil for each tenth of an ephah of flour.

chunks.en: those of a single person with those of the community,
chunks.st: And one may mix together the libations of the offering of an individual with those of a communal offering.

chunks.en: those of today with those of yesterday.
chunks.st: And one may mix together the libations of an offering brought on one day with those of the day before, if the meal offerings have the same ratio of oil to flour.

chunks.en: But we may not mix the nesachim
chunks.st: But one may not mix together the libations of

chunks.en: of lambs with the nesachim of bulls and rams.
chunks.st: lambs with the libations of bulls or the libations of rams, as the meal offerings have different ratios of oil to flour.

chunks.en: And if he mixed these by themselves
chunks.st: And nevertheless, if one intermingled the flour and oil of these lamb offerings by themselves

chunks.en: and those by themselves,
chunks.st: and the flour and oil of these bull or ram offerings by themselves,

chunks.en: and then they got mixed together, they are kosher.
chunks.st: and only then were they mixed together, then they remain fit to be sacrificed.

chunks.en: If it happened before he mixed them,
chunks.st: If they were mixed together before the oil and flour of each offering were independently intermingled to form the meal offering,

chunks.en: it is pasul. The lamb that comes with the omer,
chunks.st: then they are disqualified. With regard to the lamb offering that comes with the omer meal offering, which is accompanied by another meal offering and a wine libation,

chunks.en: even though its mincha is doubled,
chunks.st: even though the quantity of flour used in its meal offering is doubled,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one uses twice the amount that is generally used for meal offerings that accompany the sacrifice of a lamb,

chunks.en: its nesachim were not doubled.
chunks.st: its oil and wine libations were not doubled;
chunks.stMore: rather, three log of oil and three log of wine were used, per the standard quantities used for a lamb.

summary: The measuring cups were filled heaped up, except for the Kohen Gadol's. What spills over from liquid cups is holy, but not from dry cups. Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yosei give different reasons.

chunks.en: All the measures that were in the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: All measuring vessels that were in the Temple were

chunks.en: were filled heaped up,
chunks.st: such that they held the volume that they measured when their contents were heaped above the rim,

chunks.en: except for that of the Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: except for the measuring vessel used to measure the flour for the griddle-cake offering of the High Priest,

chunks.en: whose heaped amount fit inside it.
chunks.st: as its heaped measure, i.e., the quantity of flour held by a tenth of an ephah measuring vessel when heaped, was contained within its walls when the flour was leveled with the rim.
chunks.stMore: This was due to the fact that the measuring vessel for the griddle-cake offering was slightly larger than the tenth of an ephah measuring vessel.

chunks.en: The measures for liquids:
chunks.st: With regard to measuring vessels for liquids,

chunks.en: what spills over them is holy.
chunks.st: their overflows, i.e., that which flows onto the outside of vessel’s walls, are sacred, but

chunks.en: And the measures for dry things:
chunks.st: with regard to measuring vessels for dry substances,

chunks.en: what spills over them is not holy.
chunks.st: their overflows are non-sacred.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says

chunks.en: The measures for liquids are holy,
chunks.st: that the reason for this difference is that since the measuring vessels for liquids are themselves sacred,

chunks.en: so what spills over them is holy.
chunks.st: therefore their overflows are sacred,

chunks.en: And the measures for dry things are not holy,
chunks.st: and since the measuring vessels for dry substances are non-sacred,

chunks.en: so what spills over them is not holy.
chunks.st: therefore their overflows are non-sacred.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: Not because of this,
chunks.st: The difference is not due to that factor.

chunks.en: but because the liquid moves around,
chunks.st: Rather, it is because the overflow of liquid was originally inside the vessel, where it became consecrated, and was then displaced,

chunks.en: and the dry does not move around.
chunks.st: whereas the overflow of a dry substance was not displaced from inside the vessel, so it had not become consecrated.

summary: All korbanos need nesachim, except the bechor, maaser, Pesach, chatas and asham. But the chatas and asham of a metzora do need nesachim.

chunks.he: כָּל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר וְהַיָּחִיד טְעוּנִין נְסָכִים,
chunks.en: All the korbanos of the community and of a single person need nesachim,
chunks.st: All offerings, whether communal or individual, require libations, i.e., a meal offering and a wine libation,

chunks.en: except for the bechor and the maaser,
chunks.st: except for the firstborn offering, the animal tithe offering,

words.note: Every tenth animal of the flock.

chunks.en: and the Pesach, and the chatas, and the asham.
chunks.st: the Paschal offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, with which libations are not brought.

chunks.en: But the chatas of a metzora
chunks.st: But the exception to this exception is that the sin offering of a leper

chunks.en: and his asham need nesachim.
chunks.st: and his guilt offering do require libations.

summary: Korbanos of the community do not get semichah, except the bull for a mistake of the Beis Din and the goat sent away on Yom Kippur. Korbanos of one person do get semichah, except the bechor, maaser and Pesach. An heir can do semichah, bring nesachim, and make a temurah.

chunks.he: כָּל קָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר אֵין בָּהֶם סְמִיכָה,
chunks.en: All korbanos of the community have no semichah,
chunks.st: For all communal offerings there is no mitzva of placing hands on the head of the offering,

chunks.en: except for the bull that comes
chunks.st: except for the bull that comes

chunks.en: for all the mitzvos,
chunks.explain: When the Beis Din made a mistake and the people sinned.
chunks.st: to atone for a community-wide violation of any one of the mitzvot
chunks.stMore: that was perpetrated due to an erroneous ruling of the Sanhedrin, where the judges of the Sanhedrin are required to place their hands upon its head (see Leviticus 4:13–21);

chunks.en: and the goat sent away on Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: and the scapegoat
chunks.stMore: brought on Yom Kippur, upon which the High Priest places his hands (see Leviticus, chapter 16).

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.en: Also the goats for avodah zarah.
chunks.explain: When the Beis Din made a mistake about avodah zarah.
chunks.st: Also in the case of the goat that comes to atone for a community-wide perpetration of idol worship
chunks.stMore: that occurred due to an erroneous ruling of the Sanhedrin, the judges of the Sanhedrin are required to place their hands upon its head (see Numbers 15:22–26).

chunks.en: All korbanos of a single person need semichah,
chunks.st: All offerings of an individual require placing hands,

chunks.en: except for the bechor, the maaser, and the Pesach.
chunks.st: except for the firstborn offering, the animal tithe offering, and the Paschal offering. The mitzva of placing hands is performed by the owner of the offering. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: And the heir does semichah, brings nesachim, and can make a temurah.
chunks.st: And if the owner died, then the heir is regarded as the offering’s owner and so he places his hands on the offering and brings the accompanying libations. And furthermore, he can substitute a non-sacred animal for it.
chunks.stMore: Although it is prohibited to perform an act of substitution, if the owner of an offering does this, his attempt is successful to the extent that the non-sacred animal is thereby consecrated, even though the original offering also remains sacred.

summary: Everyone who brings a korban does semichah, except some people who are not obligated. Semichah is an extra part of the mitzvah; it is done on the head with two hands, in the same place as the shechitah, right before it.

chunks.en: Everyone does semichah,
chunks.st: Everyone who brings an animal offering places hands upon its head,

chunks.en: except a deaf-mute,
chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a shoteh, and a child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, a minor,

words.note: Someone whose mind does not work properly.

chunks.en: a blind person, and a non-Jew,
chunks.st: a blind person, a gentile,

chunks.en: and a slave, and a messenger,
chunks.st: a Canaanite slave, the agent of the owner of the offering who brings the offering on the owner’s behalf,

chunks.en: and a woman. And semichah
chunks.st: and a woman. And the requirement of placing hands

chunks.en: is an extra part of the mitzvah,
chunks.st: is a non-essential mitzva; therefore, failure to place hands does not prevent the owner from achieving atonement.

words.note: It does not hold back the korban.

chunks.en: done on the head,
chunks.st: The rite of placing hands is performed by leaning on the head of the offering

chunks.en: with two hands.
chunks.st: with two hands.

chunks.en: And in the place where they do semichah, they shecht,
chunks.st: And in the same location in the Temple that one places hands, one slaughters the animal.

chunks.en: and right after the semichah comes the shechitah.
chunks.st: And immediately following the rite of placing hands, the slaughter is performed.

summary: Semichah and waving each have something stricter. One partner can wave for everyone, but each one must do his own semichah. Waving is done in more kinds of cases: for one person or the community, alive or after shechitah, and even for things that are not alive.

chunks.en: Semichah is stricter than waving in one way, and waving is stricter than semichah in another way.
chunks.st: There is an aspect of greater stringency with regard to placing hands than there is with regard to waving, and there is an aspect of greater stringency with regard to waving than there is with regard to placing hands.

chunks.en: For one person may wave for all the partners,
chunks.st: The stringency with regard to placing hands is that if several people are partners in bringing an offering, one of them waves the offering on behalf of all the other partners,

chunks.en: but one person may not do semichah for all the partners.
chunks.st: but one cannot fulfill the requirement of placing hands if he alone places hands on behalf of all the other partners; rather, each member must place hands himself.

chunks.en: And waving is stricter,
chunks.st: The stringency with regard to waving is

chunks.he: שֶׁהַתְּנוּפָה נוֹהֶגֶת בְּקָרְבְּנוֹת הַיָּחִיד וּבְקָרְבְּנוֹת הַצִּבּוּר,
chunks.en: because waving applies to korbanos of one person and to korbanos of the community,
chunks.st: that waving is practiced in the cases of both offerings of an individual, e.g., peace offerings, where the breast and thigh and sacrificial portions are waved, and in the cases of communal offerings, e.g., the two lambs sacrificed on Shavuot, which are waved together with the two loaves;

chunks.en: to ones that are alive and to ones that were shechted,
chunks.st: and it is practiced both in the cases of offerings when they are alive, e.g., the guilt offering of a leper and the lambs of Shavuot, and in the cases of offerings after they are slaughtered, e.g., the breast and thigh. By contrast, placing hands is practiced with a live animal.

chunks.en: to something that has a living spirit
chunks.st: A further stringency is that waving is practiced both in the case of an item in which there is a living spirit, i.e., an animal offering,

chunks.en: and to something that has no living spirit,
chunks.st: and in the case of an item in which there is not a living spirit,
chunks.stMore: e.g., the omer offering, the sota meal offering, and the loaves accompanying a thanks offering and the ram of the nazirite,

chunks.en: which is not so with semichah.
chunks.st: whereas placing hands is only ever performed upon living beings.
